distractors.reason: 'Good' is an adjective. After the verb 'sleep' we need an adverb, so we say 'sleep well', not 'sleep good'.
'Fast' means quickly. We don't say 'sleep fast' to describe a good night's rest.
'Hard' means with great effort. We don't say 'sleep hard' in this sense; the natural phrase is 'sleep well'.

example_sentence: I always sleep ___ when my room is quiet and dark.
l1_interference: В українській мові прислівник часто стоїть перед дієсловом («добре спати»), тому учні кажуть «I well sleep» замість «I sleep well». Також «добре» часто перекладають як «good» (I sleep good). Правильно: «sleep well», прислівник іде після дієслова.
common_mistake: I well sleep / I sleep good
explanation: In English, the adverb usually comes after the verb: 'sleep well', 'work hard', 'eat slowly'. 'Good' is an adjective and does not describe verbs.

related_collocations.example: I get up early on school days.
My little brother always eats slowly.
My mother works hard every day.

memory_tip: VERB + ADVERB: the adverb comes AFTER the verb. Ukrainians often put it before the verb, so think 'sleep, then well'.
